Synthetic crude oil

This class comprises synthetic crude oil, which refers to an intermediate product that is a mixture of hydrocarbons derived from the upgrading of crude bitumen into a transportable liquid form. Synthetic crude oil contains very little sulfur (less than 0.2% by weight) compared to other light crude oils due to its processing, and has a density between 834.8 and 870.8 kg/m³ (31.0°API to 38.0°API).

Natural gas liquids (including condensate) and related products

This group comprises natural gas liquids (NGLs) and related products. NGLs are found in natural gas and include liquefied petroleum gases or LPGs (propane, butane), ethane, lease condensate, pentanes plus, among others.
Natural gas liquids (including condensate) and related products

This class comprises natural gas liquids (NGLs) and related products. NGLs are found in natural gas and include liquefied petroleum gases or LPGs (propane, butane), ethane, lease condensate, pentanes plus, among others.
Liquefied petroleum gases (LPGs)
This subclass comprises liquefied petroleum gases (LPGs) consisting primarily of propane and butane.
Propane and propane mixes

Normally straight-chain gaseous paraffinic (saturated) hydrocarbon or compound (C3H8) extracted from natural gas or refinery gas streams. It is a colourless gas that boils at a temperature of -42° Celsius. Cover propane mixes.
Butane and butane mixes

Normally straight-chain or branch-chain gaseous paraffinic hydrocarbon (C4H10) extracted from natural gas or refinery gas streams. It is a colourless gas that boils at a temperature of -1° Celsius. Covers butane mixes.
Natural gas liquids (except LPGs)
This subclass comprises natural gas liquids, except liquefied petroleum gases (LPGs), and covers lease condensate and pentanes plus.
Ethane
Straight-chain gaseous paraffinic (saturated) hydrocarbon (C2H6) extracted predominantly from natural gas streams. It is a colourless gas that boils at a temperature of -88° Celsius.
Lease condensate

Light liquid hydrocarbons recovered from lease separators or field facilities at associated and non-associated natural gas wells, mostly pentanes and heavier hydrocarbons. Normally enter the crude oil stream after production.
Pentanes plus (including plant condensate)

Mixture of mainly pentanes and heavier hydrocarbons that ordinarily contains butanes. Pentanes plus (also known as natural gasoline) is obtained from the processing of raw gas, condensate or crude oil.

Natural gas liquids other than ethane, propane and butane, and similar products.

Coal

This group comprises coal, a combustible black (hard coal) and brownish-black (brown coal) rock consisting of more than 50% by weight and more than 70% by volume of carbonaceous material. It is formed from plant remains that have been compacted, hardened and chemically altered, and metamorphosed by heat and pressure over geologic time.
Hard coal

This class comprises black coal ranked as hard coal, which includes anthracite and bituminous coal. Hard coal refers to coal of gross calorific value equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis and with a mean random reflectance of vitrinite of at least 0.6%.
Anthracite

This subclass comprises anthracite, a high rank hard, lustrous black coal destined primarily for residential and industrial (as steel making) or commercial applications. It has generally less than 10% volatile matter and a high carbon content (about 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.
Anthracite

High rank hard lustrous black coal destined primarily for residential and industrial (as steel making) or commercial applications. It has generally less than 10% volatile matter and a high carbon content (about 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.
Bituminous coal

This subclass comprises coking or metallurgical coal and other bituminous coal. Bituminous coal is a medium rank coal used for gasification, industrial coking and heat raising, and residential heat raising. It is characterized by higher volatile matter than anthracite (more than 10%) and lower carbon content (less than 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.
Coking (metallurgical) coal

Bituminous coal with a quality that allows the production of a coke suitable to support a blast furnace charge. Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.
Other bituminous coal

Other bituminous coal mainly used for steam raising purposes. It is characterized by higher volatile matter than anthracite (more than 10%) and lower carbon content (less than 90% fixed carbon). Its gross calorific value is equal to or greater than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis.
Brown coal

This class comprises softer brown coal, which includes sub-bituminous coal and lignite. Brown coal refers to coal of gross calorific value of less than 24,000 kJ/kg, on an ash-free but moist basis, and a mean random reflectance of vitrinite of less than 0.6%.
Sub-bituminous coal

This subclass comprises sub-bituminous coal, a non-agglomerating coal with a gross calorific value equal to or greater than 20,000 kJ/kg and less than 24,000 kJ/kg, containing more than 31% volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.
Sub-bituminous coal
Non-agglomerating coal with a gross calorific value equal to or greater than 20,000 kJ/kg and less than 24,000 kJ/kg, containing more than 31% volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.
Lignite
This subclass comprises lignite, a non-agglomerating coal with a gross calorific value less than 20,000 kJ/kg, containing more than 31% volatile matter on a dry mineral matter free basis.

Cannabis products

This group comprises cannabis viable seeds and vegetative plants; fresh and dried cannabis (buds and leaves); cannabis oil; other cannabis extracts and concentrates; cannabis-infused edible products; and other cannabis products n.e.c., for non-medical (recreational, wellness, lifestyle, spiritual, etc.) and medical uses. A plant of the genus Cannabis refers generally to three varieties which are cannabis Sativa, cannabis Indica and cannabis Ruderalis. Sativas and Indicas are the most commonly used cannabis strains for cultivation and propagation. The genetics of the different cannabis strains are widely mixed or cloned to create cannabis hybrids. Cannabis contains a number of active elements, including cannabinoids such as tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) or dronabinol, cannabidiol (CBD) and terpenes (aromatic compounds or chemical markers). Cannabis plants containing 0.3% w/w (weight for weight) of THC or less in the flowering tops and leaves - industrial hemp - and their derivatives with the THC concentration of 10 µg/g or less, as well as prescription drugs or pharmaceuticals containing cannabis, are excluded from this group.

Cannabis seeds and vegetative plants are commonly from three varieties which are cannabis Sativa, cannabis Indica and cannabis Ruderalis. Prefabricated buildings and components thereof

This group comprises prefabricated buildings that are built in a factory or manufacturing facility and delivered to the construction site, and the components of prefabricated buildings built in a factory to be assembled later at a construction site. Prefabricated (factory-built) buildings are virtually complete and either unassembled or fully assembled (or manufactured) and ready to use; they can also be incomplete buildings, whether or not assembled, having the essential character of factory-built or prefabricated buildings. Prefabricated buildings can be used for residential or non-residential purposes. A building refers to any roofed independent free-standing permanent construction or structure usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof and comprises one or more rooms or other space. A building can be entered or accessed by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building can also include a separately usable underground construction. A residential building refers to a construction in which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or dwelling purposes. A non-residential building refers to a construction in which more than half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for non-residential purposes.
Prefabricated metal buildings and other non-wood buildings, and components thereof

This class comprises prefabricated buildings, predominantly made of metal and other non-wood material, and their components, except manufactured (mobile) buildings. Prefabricated (factory-built) metal and non-wood buildings are virtually complete and unassembled; they can also be incomplete buildings, whether or not assembled, having the essential character of factory-built or prefabricated buildings, and delivered to the construction site. Components of these buildings are built in a factory to be assembled later at a construction site. Prefabricated buildings can be used for residential or non-residential purposes.

This subclass comprises transportation of small packages and documents without tracking of each package and document. Service is typically station-to-station but may be door-to-door. May include declared value coverage.

This subclass comprises transportation and delivery, by a definite day and possibly by a definite time, of small packages and documents, with tracking of each package and document. Delivery by the scheduled day or specified time may be guaranteed. Small packages usually can be handled by one person without using special equipment. Service is typically door-to-door, although there may be options for the shipper to drop a package off and for the receiver to pick it up, and occasional shippers may have to drop off their packages. Residential buildings

This group comprises residential buildings. A residential building refers to a construction in which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or private dwelling purposes, whether on a permanent basis or not. Residential buildings normally provide accommodation units or residential building units with self-contained and exclusive use of bathroom and kitchen facilities to the occupants of each unit. At least half of the useful floor area must be used or intended for dwelling units, in the case of apartment buildings. A residential building unit is a structurally separated and independent place. A group of three row houses that are attached is considered to be three separate buildings if their external walls or dividing walls extend from the foundations to the roof. Residential buildings constructed entirely at the building site, as well as on-site fully assembled precast, panelized, modular and other prefabricated residential buildings are included in this group. Unassembled prefabricated residential buildings built in a factory, and manufactured or fully assembled residential buildings built in a factory and delivered ready for move-in, are excluded from this group. A building for which the majority of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for dwelling units with shared bathroom and kitchen, or that area is used primarily to offer care and other assisted living services, is classified as a "collective dwelling-type building" under the non-residential buildings group. A building refers to any independent free-standing permanent structure comprising one or more residential dwelling units, business units or other spaces. A building can be entered by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building is covered by a roof and is usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof. In the case of interconnected structures (e.g., semi-detached or terraced houses), any unit separated from other units by a fire wall extending from roof to cellar is considered an individual building. If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access (own entrance) as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.

If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access (own entrance) as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.
Residential buildings of five or more storeys

This subclass comprises residential buildings of five or more storeys. A residential building of five or more storeys refers to such a building of which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or dwelling purposes. A residential building also generally provides accommodation units with self-contained and exclusive use of bathroom and kitchen facilities to the occupants of the apartments, condominiums or other types of dwellings in the building. These types of buildings do not provide care or other assisted daily living services; they provide private dwellings for at least half of the overall useful floor area of the building.

Residential buildings of fewer than five storeys

This subclass comprises residential buildings of fewer than five storeys. A residential building of five or more storeys refers to such a building of which at least half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for residential or dwelling purposes. A residential building also generally provides accommodation units with self-contained and exclusive use of bathroom and kitchen facilities to the occupants of the apartments, condominiums or other types of dwellings in the building. These types of buildings do not provide care or other assisted daily living services; they provide private dwellings for at least half of the overall useful floor area of the building.
Single-detached houses
Single dwellings not attached to any other dwelling or structure (except their own garage or shed) that have open space on all sides and have no dwellings either above them or below them.
Semi-detached houses

Two dwellings attached side by side (or back to back) to each other, but not attached to any other dwelling or structure (except their own garage or shed), that have no dwellings either above them or below them. The two units together have open space on all sides.
Row houses

Row houses refer to row of three or more attached, one-family dwellings, each built with similar architectural treatment, separated by vertical divisions termed "party" or "lot-line" walls, and each having private entrances (usually both front and rear). Also a group of apartments, usually row-oriented, where each one is like a separate "house" and is usually two storeys. It generally refers to such units in an urban area and they are often condominiums. Often referred to as "townhouses".

Non-residential buildings

This group comprises non-residential buildings. A non-residential building refers to a construction in which more than half of the overall useful floor area is used or intended for non-residential purposes, namely for industrial, commercial or institutional purposes, including for the provision of services. A non-residential building unit is a structurally separated and independent place. Non-residential buildings constructed entirely at the building site, as well as on-site fully assembled precast, panelized, modular and other prefabricated non-residential buildings are included in this group. Unassembled prefabricated non-residential buildings built in a factory, and manufactured or fully assembled non-residential buildings built in a factory and delivered ready for move-in, are excluded from this group. A building for which more than half of the useful floor area is used or intended for dwelling units or accommodation units with shared bathroom and kitchen, or that area is used primarily to offer care and other assisted living services, is classified as a "collective dwelling-type building" in this group. A building refers to any roofed independent free-standing permanent construction or structure usually enclosed within external walls or dividing walls that extend from the foundations to the roof and comprises one or more rooms or other space. A building can be entered or accessed by persons or animals and is suitable or intended for protecting them and objects. A building can also include a separately usable underground construction. In the case of interconnected structures, any unit separated from other units by a fire wall extending from roof to cellar is considered an individual building. If there is no fire wall, the interconnected building units are regarded as individual buildings if they have their own access or entrance, as well as their own utility system and are separately usable.

Research and experimental development services

This group comprises research and experimental development services in natural sciences, engineering and technology, medical and health sciences, agricultural and veterinary sciences, social sciences, and humanities and the arts. Research and experimental development (R&D) comprise creative and systemic work undertaken in order to increase the stock of knowledge - including knowledge of humankind, culture and society - and to devise new applications of available knowledge. The term R&D refers to three types of activity: basic research, applied research and experimental development. Basic research refers to experimental or theoretical work undertaken primarily to acquire new knowledge of the underlying foundations of phenomena and observable facts, without any particular application or use in view. Applied research refers to original investigation undertaken in order to acquire new knowledge. It is, however, directed primarily towards a specific, practical aim or objective. Experimental development is systematic work, drawing on knowledge gained from research and practical experience and producing additional knowledge, which is directed to producing new products or processes or to improving existing products or processes.
Research and experimental developmental services in natural sciences

This class comprises research and experimental development services in natural sciences. Natural sciences refers to scientific disciplines concerned with understanding, exploring or developing the natural world. Research services consist of systematic investigation carried by means of experiment or analysis to achieve a scientific or technological advance such as acquiring new knowledge of the underlying foundation of phenomena and observable facts. Experimental development services consist of new or substantially improved goods, services, systems, methods or processes.

Telecommunications, broadcasting distribution and related services

This group comprises fixed wholesale and retail telecommunications services; fixed wholesale and retail Internet access services; mobile wholesale and retail telecommunications services; cable, satellite, Internet and other fixed or mobile broadcasting distribution services of audiovisual and audio works; and online games, except gambling.
Wholesale telecommunications services (carrier services)
This class comprises fixed wholesale telecommunications and Internet access services, and mobile wholesale telecommunications.
Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)

This subclass comprises the provision of a fixed telecommunications service or facility by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of retail fixed telecommunications services. The purchaser may resell the service or facility to another entity, or use the service or facility to support the services it bills.
Fixed wholesale telecommunications services (except Internet access)

Provision of a fixed telecommunications service or facility by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of retail fixed telecommunications services. The purchaser may resell the service or facility to another entity, or use the service or facility to support the services it bills.
Fixed wholesale Internet access services
This subclass comprises the provision of fixed Internet access and transport services by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of fixed retail Internet access services.
Fixed wholesale Internet access services
Provision of fixed Internet access and transport services by a telecommunications service provider to a provider of fixed retail Internet access services.
Mobile wholesale telecommunications services

This subclass comprises the provision of a mobile telecommunications service or facility by a wireless telecommunications service provider to another to exchange traffic and extend service coverage area.
Mobile wholesale telecommunications services
Provision of a mobile telecommunications service or facility by a wireless telecommunications service provider to another to exchange traffic and extend service coverage area.
Retail telecommunication services
This class comprises fixed retail telecommunications and Internet access services, and mobile retail telecommunications.
Fixed retail telecommunications services (except Internet access)
This subclass comprises telephone services to end users where calls originate from a device connected to a landline.
Fixed local and access telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
A landline-based telephone service that allows end users to make calls within a defined local area and provides access to a long distance network of the customer's choice.
Fixed long distance telecommunications services (except Internet access), at retail
A landline-based telephone service allowing end users to make calls outside a local calling area.
Data transmission services
Telecommunications services making use of data protocols to transmit data over a public network.
Private network services
Telecommunications network segments for the exclusive use of the client on which no control or signalling is performed by the telecommunications service provider.
Fixed retail Internet access services
This subclass comprises the provision of fixed connections (including fixed wireline and wireless) to the Internet to end users.
Dial-up Internet access services

Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to end users at download speeds not exceeding 64 Kbps. Dial-up Internet access is one of the oldest forms of Internet access technology. It is also referred to as low or narrowband speed Internet access. Narrowband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of up to 1.5 Mbps.
Fixed high-speed Internet access services, residential

Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to residential end users at download speeds generally greater than 256 Kbps. High-speed Internet is also referred to as broadband Internet, with fixed line types such as cable, digital subscriber line (DSL), terrestrial wireless access, direct-to-home satellite access, and fibre optic services. Even though the lowest speed limit for high-speed Internet is set to 256 Kbps in several countries, broadband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of 1.5 Mbps or greater. Connection with download speed from 256 Kbps up to 1.5 Mbps is sometimes referred to as "wideband" or "lite broadband".
Fixed high-speed Internet access services, non-residential

Provision of fixed connections to the Internet to non-residential or business end users at download speeds greater than 256 Kbps. High-speed Internet is also referred to as broadband Internet, with fixed line types such as cable, digital subscriber line (DSL), terrestrial wireless access, direct-to-home satellite access, and fibre optic services. Even though the lowest speed limit for high-speed Internet is set to 256 Kbps in several countries, broadband is generally regarded as a category including any connection with a transmission or download speed of 1.5 Mbps or greater. Connection with download speed from 256 Kbps up to 1.5 Mbps is sometimes referred to as "wideband" or "lite broadband".
Mobile retail telecommunications services
This subclass comprises telecommunication services to end users where voice or data communications originate from, or terminate into, a mobile device connected to a wireless network.
Mobile local and access telecommunications services, at retail

A wireless-based telecommunications service that allows end users to make and receive calls within a defined local area and provides access to a long distance network of the customer's choice. Mobile cell phone plans typically bundle voice and text messaging.
Mobile long distance telecommunications services, at retail
Wireless based telecommunications service allowing end users to make calls outside a local calling area.
Mobile data services

A service plan providing end users mobile access to text and multimedia messaging, along with access to the Internet through the cellular network. This service is also referred as "wireless mobile Internet access", at retail.
Roaming services
A service that allows a cell phone subscriber to use his or her mobile device while in the service area of another service provider.
Broadcasting and online games distribution services

This class comprises broadcast distribution services of audiovisual and audio works such as television programs, films, videos, sound recordings, via cable, satellite, Internet and other fixed and mobile distribution streams. Also covers distribution services for online games, except gambling, and installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks.
Basic television programming packages
This subclass comprises basic television programming packages distribution services, via fixed or mobile devices.
Basic television programming packages (except online streaming)

Providing a basic package of movie and television programming services, basically to a fixed device, except using online streaming, for a monthly subscription fee. Basic packages are any first level programming package that must be purchased before being able to purchase additional programming packages. The basic programming packages are delivered using traditional over-the-air (OTA), cable and satellite television.
Online streaming of basic programming packages

Providing a basic package of movie and television programming services over the Internet, to a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming, for a monthly subscription fee. Basic packages are any first level programming package that must be purchased before being able to purchase additional programming packages.
Discretionary television programming packages
This subclass comprises discretionary television programming packages distribution services, via fixed or mobile devices.
Discretionary programming packages (except online streaming)

Providing movie and television programming services, in addition to those included in a basic package, for an additional monthly subscription fee, generally to a fixed device, except using online streaming. This programming service comprises bundles of channels or à la carte channels. The discretionary television programming packages are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.
Online streaming of discretionary programming packages

Providing movie and television programming services over the Internet, in addition to those included in a basic package, for an additional monthly subscription fee, to a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming. This programming service comprises bundles of channels or à la carte channels.
Pay-per-view services
This subclass comprises pay-per-view services, via fixed or mobile devices. The broadcaster shows a pay-per-view program at the same broadcast time to everyone ordering it.
Pay-per-view services (except online streaming)

Providing services which enable subscribers to television programming packages, to watch a specific program (movie or event) at the same broadcast time, generally at a fixed device, for an additional fee, except using online streaming. The pay-per-view services are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.
Online streaming of pay-per-view programs

Providing services over the Internet which enable subscribers to television programming packages, to watch a specific program (movie or event) at the same broadcast time, on a fixed or mobile device, using online streaming, for an additional fee.
Television, movie and video on demand services

This subclass comprises pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except pay-per-view), via fixed or mobile devices. Subscribers or viewers of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, for a one time fee paid for each individual video that is on demand (transactional video on demand), or for a monthly or annual subscription fee (subscription video on demand) to have unlimited access to television programs, movies and any other types of videos during the time covered by the subscription.
Television, movie and video on demand (except online streaming)

Providing pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except per-pay-view), generally via fixed devices, except using online streaming. Subscribers or viewers to/of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, usually for a one time fee paid for each individual video that is on demand (transactional video on demand). Video on demand services are delivered using traditional cable and satellite television.
Online on demand streaming of television, movie and video

Providing pay television, movie and other video on demand services (except pay-per-view) over the Internet, via fixed or mobile devices, using online streaming. Subscribers or viewers to/of video on demand are allowed to choose and watch broadcasts at any time, usually for a monthly or annual subscription fee (subscription video on demand) to have unlimited access to television programs, movies and any other types of videos during the time covered by the subscription.
Satellite radio and online audio streaming services
This subclass comprises pay satellite radio and online audio (such as music) streaming services.
Satellite radio services
Pay satellite radio services.
Online audio streaming services

Providing programming services (including self-programming), over the Internet, that comprise a single payment (fee) or a subscription, to a selection of radio shows, music and other audio recordings, streamed to fixed and mobile devices (Internet audio services). Subscribers are allowed to choose and stream contents at any time during the time covered by the payment or subscription.
Online gaming services (except gambling)

This subclass comprises provision of various games to be played online, on a subscription or single payment (fee) basis, except gambling. The games are streamed over the Internet to fixed and mobile devices.
Online gaming services (except gambling)
Providing various games to be played online, on a subscription or single payment (fee) basis, except gambling. The games are streamed over the Internet to fixed and mobile devices.

Installation services for connections to broadcasting distribution networks
Providing installation of cables on the customer premises and/or installing outlets to connect to the program or broadcasting distribution networks.

Services that analyze the way a business process is conducted, and identifies improvements that can be made by integrating existing and new software services, in order to improve information flows and increase automation of the process.

This subclass comprises other information technology (IT) hosting or infrastructure provisioning services such as hosting client's application, processing client's data and computer time share.

Data management infrastructure provisioning services
Services of providing the infrastructure and on-going management and administration of data as an organizational resource.

Infrastructure as a service (except data storage infrastructure provisioning)
Infrastructure as a service (except data storage infrastructure provisioning).

Platform as a service (PaaS), or application platform as a service (aPaaS), refers to a category of cloud computing services that allows customers to provision, run, and manage a modular bundle of one or more applications and based on IT infrastructure as a service.
Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services, n.e.c.
Other information technology (IT) infrastructure provisioning services, n.e.c.

This subclass comprises the service of managing and monitoring a client's information technology (IT) infrastructure including hardware, software and networks.

Services of managing and monitoring communication networks and connected hardware to diagnose networking problems and gather capacity and usage statistics for the administration and fine-tuning of network traffic.

Services of converting paper documents into digital or other machine-readable formats. Other information services
This subclass comprises other information services.

Providing access to archives, and other archive-related services.

Deposit account service packages

Credit card products

This subclass comprises the provision of lines of credit to credit card holders, and credit card processing services to merchants, that together enable credit cards to be accepted as a means of payment.
Credit card cardholder products for businesses and government

Provision of a revolving line of credit to business and government holders of credit cards, allowing them to purchase goods and services from merchants who accept their card. Credit granted through credit cards may be unsecured, or secured by a deposit held by the card issuer.
Credit card cardholder products to consumers

Provision of a revolving line of credit to consumer holders of credit cards, allowing them to purchase goods and services from merchants who accept their card. Credit granted through credit cards may be unsecured, or secured by a deposit held by the card issuer.
Credit card merchant products
Credit card transaction processing services provided by processors and banks to merchant account holders.
Credit card association products
Services provided by credit card associations to issuing banks.
Factoring

This subclass comprises the provision of financing to a business from the sale of its accounts receivable to a third party, known as a factor. Normally, the factor assumes the full risk of collection, including credit losses.
Factoring
Financing provided to a business from the sale of its accounts receivable to a third party, known as a factor. Normally, the factor assumes the full risk of collection, including credit losses.
Financial leasing

This subclass comprises leases in which the lessor is providing a financial service to enable the lessee to enjoy the benefits of ownership of the leased asset. A lessee has the option of purchasing the machinery and equipment after the lease term has been completed, at an agreed price. With a finance lease the equipment appears on the lessee's balance sheet, as it is viewed as a purchase. Also known as capital lease.
Financial leasing, motor vehicles

Motor vehicle leases in which the lessor is providing a financial service to enable the lessee to enjoy the benefits of ownership of the leased asset. A lessee has the option of purchasing the motor vehicle after the lease term has been completed, at an agreed price. With a finance lease the motor vehicle appears on the lessee's balance sheet, as it is viewed as a purchase.
Financial leasing (except motor vehicles)

Leases (except for motor vehicles) in which the lessor is providing a financial service to enable the lessee to enjoy the benefits of ownership of the leased asset. A lessee has the option of purchasing the machinery and equipment after the lease term has been completed, at an agreed price. With a finance lease the equipment appears on the lessee's balance sheet, as it is viewed as a purchase.

Sales financing to consumers

Other credit financing products
